questions.q: What did Ahithophel advise Absalom and all the elders of Israel about how he should attack David?
questions.a: Ahithophel’s advice was to let him lead a large army carry out a surprise attack on David that night, when he was weary and weak, kill only David, and bring back all the rest of the people for Absalom to rule.

questions.q: What was Hushai’s opinion of Ahithophel’s plan?
questions.a: Hushai said that the counsel Ahithophel had given on this occasion was not good.

questions.q: Why did Hushai say the plan was not good?
questions.a: Hushai said that David and his very brave warriors were probably in a safe place, and David’s soldiers will certainly kill some of Ahithophel’s soldiers at the start of the battle. When people hear about that, they will say that David’s soldiers are slaughtering Absalom’s soldiers! Then your other soldiers, even if they are as fearless as lions, will become very afraid.

questions.q: What did Hushai advise Absalom to do?
questions.a: Hushai advised Absalom to gather all of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and for Absalom himself to go into the battle. He said that this great army would overwhelm David’s smaller army and none of them would survive.

questions.q: How did Absalom and the men of Israel respond to Hushai’s advice?
questions.a: They said the counsel of Hushai was better than the counsel of Ahithophel and they decided to do what Hushai suggested.

questions.q: What message did Hushai send to David?
questions.a: The message was that David should not stay at the place where people can walk across the Jordan River but should cross over immediately, because otherwise, Absalom and his army may come and kill them.

questions.q: How was information relayed to King David?
questions.a: A maidservant of the two priests would go and declare news to Jonathan and Ahimaaz, and they would go and declare it to King David.

questions.q: What did Jonathan and Ahimaaz do when a young man saw them and told Absalom?
questions.a: The two of them went quickly to the house of a man in Bahurim and went down into a well in his courtyard.

questions.q: How were the two men helped?
questions.a: The man’s wife spread a covering over the well and spread grain on it, and when Absalom’s servants asked where the men were, she told them they had crossed the brook.

questions.q: After Absalom’s men left, what did the two men do?
questions.a: They came up from the well, went and reported the news to King David, and told him to get all these people across the Jordan River quickly.

questions.q: What did Ahithophel do when he saw that his counsel was not followed?
questions.a: Ahithophel saddled his donkey, went to his house, gave to his family instructions about what to do with his possessions, and then he hanged himself because he knew that otherwise David would kill him as a traitor.

questions.q: How were David and his people cared for in the wilderness?
questions.a: Shobi, Machir, and Barzillai brought beds, basins, pottery, and all kinds of food for David and the people with him to eat.

commentary.text: He hangs himself, Absalom pursues David.

Verses 1–21 Here was a wonderful effect of Divine Providence blinding Absalom's mind and influencing his heart, that he could not rest in Ahithophel's counsel, and that he should desire Hushai's advice. But there is no contending with that God who can arm a man against himself, and destroy him by his own mistakes and passions. Ahithophel's former counsel was followed, for God intended to correct David; but his latter counsel was not followed, for God meant not to destroy him. He can overrule all counsels. Whatever wisdom or help any man employs or affords, the success is from God alone, who will not let his people perish.

Ahithophel hanged himself for vexation that his counsel was not followed. That will break a proud man's heart which will not break a humble man's sleep. He thought himself in danger, concluding, that, because his counsel was not followed, Absalom's cause would fail; and to prevent a possible public execution, he does justice upon himself. Thus the breath is stopped, and the head laid low, from which nothing could be expected but mischief. Absalom chased his father. But observe how God sometimes makes up to his people that comfort from strangers, which they are disappointed of in their own families. Our King needs not our help; but he assures us, that what we do for the least of his brethren, who are sick, poor, and destitute, shall be accepted and recompensed as if done to himself
